info.title: Juno Public API
info.description: The private-beta Juno API for AI-moderated research. A developer briefs Juno on a user's behalf; Juno creates a study in Test mode, where the user can simulate the interview shape without credits, analysis, or exports. The user selects Go live for real participant interviews in Live mode, where credits are deducted and analysis and exports are available. Each study has one durable invite link. API keys are not self-service during the private beta; Juno issues org-scoped keys (jsk_live_… / jsk_test_…) to approved developers. Request access at https://support.heyjuno.co.

get.description:
Verify a Juno-issued key and see what it can do: its organisation, API
data environment, and scopes. The key environment is separate from a
study's Test mode or Live mode. Any valid key may call this; no specific
scope is required.

List your organisation's studies, newest created first. A study is one
research project: an AI-moderated interview Juno designs and runs, plus the
analysis built from the answers. Page with the cursor from the X-Next-Cursor
response header, which is absent on the last page.

schema.description: Opaque cursor from the previous page's X-Next-Cursor header. Omit for the first page. Cursors are keyset-based, so rows arriving mid-pagination never shift or duplicate the page you are walking.
schema.title: Cursor
Response List Studies V1 Api Studies Get

post.description:
Brief Juno to create a research study from plain-language guidance:
describe what the user wants to learn, and Juno designs the interview — objectives, screener
questions, and the questions the interviewer will ask. Upload documents
first and include their file_ids when they are part of the brief. Authoring runs in
the background: this returns a job_id; poll Check authoring status
until the study and its brief are ready. New studies start in test mode so
the user can safely simulate the shape of the interview before choosing
Go live. Test mode uses no credits, provides no analysis or exports,
and is not intended for real participant research.

get.description:
Fetch one study, including its current brief — the study design Juno
authored: title, objectives, and the questions the interviewer asks. The
brief is null until an authoring job has completed.

Get the study's invite link — the durable URL the user shares with
participants. In Test mode it opens the safe preview experience; after the
user selects Go live, it admits real participants to Live mode.

post.description:
Create an invite link carrying what you already know about the people who
will open it — company, role, the systems they use. Juno briefs the
interviewer with it, so the interview does not ask for details you supplied.

By default the link is for a **group**: send one link to everyone in that
segment. Set `audience` to `person` when the context identifies one
individual and you want the finished interview matched back to their record;
that link then belongs to whoever opens it first. The context is recorded on
the resulting interview and returned by List interviews.

Upload background material for Create a study or Update a study.
The returned file_id has no effect by itself; include it in file_ids
when creating or updating the study. Supports PDF, DOCX, TXT, and MD.

get.description:
Track a study Juno is authoring. Creating or refining a study returns a
job_id; poll this endpoint until status is ready, at which
point study_id and the authored brief (title, objectives, and
interview questions) are populated. failed means authoring did not
complete — brief Juno again.

post.description:
Update a study with further plain-language instructions from the user —
in Test mode or Live mode. The technical :refine path and
refine_study operation name are retained for wire compatibility. Each
update creates a new design version. Upload new documents first and include
their file_ids when they are part of the update. Returns a job_id; poll Check
authoring status like a fresh authoring run.

In Test mode, simulate the interview before the user selects Go live:
Juno plays both sides — the
interviewer runs the study's real interview, and a synthetic participant
answers it — producing a sample transcript. Optionally steer the
participant with a persona description. Simulation runs in the
background: this returns a job_id; poll Check a simulation to watch
the transcript grow turn by turn. Simulation uses no credits, provides no
analysis or exports, and is not real participant research. The current
endpoint does not enforce mode=test; developers must treat that as the
product contract.

get.description:
Track a simulation started with Simulate an interview and read its
sample transcript. The response carries the turns produced so far, so you
can render the conversation while it runs; once status is
completed the transcript is final. Simulated interviews are a Test-mode
action — they are never counted, analysed, or exported as real interviews.

List participant interviews, newest first — the endpoint to poll to learn
when interviews happen. Each entry carries the interview's state, timings,
and the values captured from the participant's invite link, plus a link into
Juno; transcripts and participant identity are deliberately not included.
Filter by study_id and by status, and page with the cursor from the
X-Next-Cursor response header (absent on the last page). Check is_test
before acting on an interview: Test-mode rehearsals appear here too.

schema.description: Only return interviews belonging to this study.

Response List Interviews V1 Api Interviews Get

get.description:
Fetch one interview by id. Same projection as List interviews: state,
timings, invite-link values, and a permalink — no transcript or participant
identity. Use Start an export for the full transcript data.

put.description:
Map the established mode wire field onto the product lifecycle.
test selects Test mode: simulate the interview shape with no credits,
analysis, or exports and no real participant research. live selects
Live mode: real participant interviews deduct credits and enable analysis
and exports. The user-facing action is Go live. The same field retains
paused and closed as technical collection states. Going live the
first time runs validation and requires studies:golive; other changes
require studies:write. Repeating the current value is a no-op.

post.description:
In Live mode, export completed participant interviews as CSV —
transcripts and answers with the organisation's PII-redaction settings
applied. Test-mode simulations cannot be exported. Exports run in the
background: this returns a job_id; poll Check export status, then
fetch the file from Download an export once ready.

get.description:
Track an export started with Start an export. Poll until ready is
true, then fetch the file from Download an export. failed means the
export did not complete — start a new one.

Fetch the finished export file: a short-lived signed URL to the CSV
(redaction preserved), or the CSV streamed inline where object storage is
not configured. Responds 409 until the export is ready — poll Check
export status first.

job_id.title: Job Id
job_id.description: Authoring job handle. Poll GET /v1/api/studies/jobs/{job_id} until status is 'ready'.

thread_id.title: Thread Id
thread_id.description: The authoring conversation thread the run executes in.

AuthoringJobOut.title: AuthoringJobOut
AuthoringJobOut.description: 202 acceptance handle. ``job_id`` is the chat run id == DBOS workflow id.

study_id.title: Study Id
study_id.description: The study the job created or updated, once one exists.

brief.description: The current brief, once authored and ready to review.

objectives.title: Objectives
objectives.description: What the study sets out to learn, as researcher-legible statements.

pre_interview_questions.title: Pre Interview Questions
pre_interview_questions.description: Questions asked before the interview starts (screeners).

verbatim_questions.title: Verbatim Questions
verbatim_questions.description: Questions the interviewer asks word for word during the interview.

estimated_duration_minutes.title: Estimated Duration Minutes
estimated_duration_minutes.description: Planned interview length in minutes, when the design specifies one.

Brief.title: Brief
Brief.description:
Lean, non-leaky projection of the study's brief — Juno's authored design.

The same noun the app uses (the Brief tab). Never carries ``design_json``,
``interpreted_brief``, or brand config — only the researcher-legible
surface.

ExportFormat.title: ExportFormat
ExportFormat.description: Supported export formats. Start with interviews CSV; extend as needed.

job_id.title: Job Id
job_id.description: Export job handle. Poll GET /v1/api/exports/{job_id} until ready.

ExportJobAccepted.title: ExportJobAccepted
ExportJobAccepted.description: 202 acceptance handle. ``job_id`` addresses the async export job.

ready.title: Ready
ready.description: True only when the artifact is downloadable from GET /v1/api/exports/{job_id}/download.

ExportJobStatus.title: ExportJobStatus
ExportJobStatus.description:
Derived job status. ``status`` ∈ {queued, running, completed, failed}.

``ready`` is ``True`` only when the artifact is downloadable (status
``completed``), so callers can poll on a single boolean.

study_id.title: Study Id
study_id.description: Study whose Live-mode participant interviews to export.

format.description: Export format. Only 'csv' is supported today.

ExportRequest.title: ExportRequest
ExportRequest.description: Instruction to start an async export for one of the caller's studies.

file_id.title: File Id
file_id.description: Use as a file_ids entry when creating or updating a study.

extracted.title: Extracted
extracted.description: Whether text was parsed out of the file. False for empty or binary types that carry no extractable content.

FileUploadOut.title: FileUploadOut
FileUploadOut.description:
Lean handle for an uploaded guidance file.

``file_id`` has no effect until it is used in ``file_ids`` when creating or
updating a study. ``extracted`` reports whether text was parsed out of the
file (false for empty/binary types that carry no extractable content).

url.title: Url
url.description: Absolute invite URL (e.g. https://www.heyjuno.co/chat/{token}). The user shares it with participants; it is durable across lifecycle changes.

mode.title: Mode
mode.description: The study's lifecycle value at the time of this response. Advisory only — participant behavior follows the value when they open the link.

InterviewLinkOut.title: InterviewLinkOut
InterviewLinkOut.description:
The study's single durable invite link, plus its current lifecycle value.

The URL never changes as the study moves through its lifecycle. In Test mode
it supports previewing; after Go live it admits real participants to Live
mode. ``mode`` here is point-in-time information, not a property of the link.

url.title: Url
url.description: Absolute invite URL. The context you supplied is stored against the link rather than written into it, so the URL reveals nothing about who it is for. Treat it as sensitive: anyone holding it arrives carrying the context.

audience.title: Audience
audience.description: The audience this link was minted for. 'group' is reusable — send it to as many people as you like. 'person' addresses one interview; reopening the same link continues that interview, so give each different participant a fresh link.

mode.title: Mode
mode.description: The study's lifecycle value when the link was minted. Advisory only — participant behavior follows the value when they open it.

ParticipantLinkOut.title: ParticipantLinkOut
ParticipantLinkOut.description: An invite URL and the audience it was minted for.

context.title: Context
context.description: Key/value facts about the people this link is for, e.g. {"company": "Coca-Cola", "role": "Head of Martech"}. At most 20 keys; keys up to 100 characters, values up to 2048, 16KB total.

audience.title: Audience
audience.description: Who the link is for. 'group' (the default) describes a segment — everyone you send it to gets this context, so one link covers a whole company or role. Use 'person' when the context identifies one individual (e.g. a contact_id you want the finished interview matched back to): the link then addresses one interview. Reopening that same link continues the interview with its original context, even in another browser or device. Give each different participant a fresh person link and treat it as sensitive.

note.title: Note
note.description: Free-text direction for the interviewer about the people this link is for, e.g. 'These participants recently cancelled. Explore what changed and why they left.' Unlike context (facts, which become data columns on the interview), the note is guidance Juno follows during the conversation. Up to 2048 characters. Never shown to the participant and never included in exports.

ParticipantLinkRequest.title: ParticipantLinkRequest
ParticipantLinkRequest.description:
Context to attach to an invite link, and who the link is for.

Values become the interview's entry attributes: recorded on the interview
row, shown in the interviews table and exports, and — excluding campaign
attribution — briefed to the interviewer as established fact so it does not
ask the participant for details you already supplied.

id.title: Id
id.description: Unique interview id, stable for the life of the interview. Use it to deduplicate when polling.

study_id.title: Study Id
study_id.description: The study this interview belongs to.

status.title: Status
status.description: 'in_progress' while the participant is still going, 'completed' once the interview ended normally, 'failed' if it errored out.

is_complete.title: Is Complete
is_complete.description: True only for 'completed'. Convenient for filtering in one field.

is_test.title: Is Test
is_test.description: True for Test-mode interviews, which are rehearsals rather than real participant research. Check this before acting on an interview — test runs use no credits and are not real data.

started_at.title: Started At
started_at.description: When the interview record was created.

completed_at.title: Completed At
completed_at.description: When the interview ended. Null while still in progress.

duration_seconds.title: Duration Seconds
duration_seconds.description: Active participant time in seconds, excluding pauses. Null until the runtime has measured any.

entry_attributes.title: Entry Attributes
entry_attributes.description: Values captured from the participant's invite link — whatever the caller attached when inviting them (a CRM contact id, company, role). The intended way to match an interview back to the record it came from.

invite_audience.title: Invite Audience
invite_audience.description: Audience of the contextual participant link used to start this interview: 'group' or 'person'. Null when the interview came from the study's plain link or predates participant-link attribution.

permalink.title: Permalink
permalink.description: Absolute URL that opens this interview's transcript in Juno.

PublicInterview.title: PublicInterview
PublicInterview.description:
One participant interview, as metadata plus a link back into Juno.

Deliberately carries no transcript, answers, or participant identity: an
integration forwards this into third-party systems, and a participant
consented to research with Juno, not to their answers being syndicated.
Correlation is meant to run through ``entry_attributes`` — the caller's own
identifiers, which they attached to the invite link themselves.

id.title: Id
id.description: Unique study id. Use it in every study-scoped call.

name.title: Name
name.description: Human-readable study name, as shown in the Juno app.

mode.title: Mode
mode.description: Current lifecycle value. 'test' means Test mode: the user can simulate the interview shape with no credits, analysis, or exports; it is not for real participant research. 'live' means Live mode: real participant interviews deduct credits and enable analysis and exports. 'paused' and 'closed' are technical collection states. Use PUT /v1/api/studies/{study_id}/mode; mode='live' is the API equivalent of the user selecting Go live.

launched_at.title: Launched At
launched_at.description: When the study first went live. Null if it never has.

brief.description: The study's current brief. Null only while nothing has been authored yet (an authoring job is still working).

PublicStudyDetail.title: PublicStudyDetail
PublicStudyDetail.description:
One study together with its current brief.

``brief`` is the same lean projection the authoring-status endpoint
reports; it is ``None`` only while nothing has been authored yet.

id.title: Id
id.description: Unique study id. Use it in every study-scoped call.

name.title: Name
name.description: Human-readable study name, as shown in the Juno app.

mode.title: Mode
mode.description: Current lifecycle value. 'test' means Test mode: the user can simulate the interview shape with no credits, analysis, or exports; it is not for real participant research. 'live' means Live mode: real participant interviews deduct credits and enable analysis and exports. 'paused' and 'closed' are technical collection states. Use PUT /v1/api/studies/{study_id}/mode; mode='live' is the API equivalent of the user selecting Go live.

launched_at.title: Launched At
launched_at.description: When the study first went live. Null if it never has.

PublicStudySummary.title: PublicStudySummary
PublicStudySummary.description:
Stable, non-leaky projection of a study for the public API.

``mode`` is the established collapsed lifecycle field. ``test``/``live``
map to Test mode/Live mode; ``paused``/``closed`` are collection states.
``launched_at`` being non-null means the study has been live at least once.
Internal design/brief/brand JSON is never surfaced here.

job_id.title: Job Id
job_id.description: Simulation job handle. Poll GET /v1/api/simulations/{job_id} to watch the transcript grow and to learn when it completes.

SimulationJobAccepted.title: SimulationJobAccepted
SimulationJobAccepted.description: 202 acceptance handle. ``job_id`` addresses the async simulation job.

persona.title: Persona
persona.description: Optional plain-language description of the synthetic participant (e.g. 'a skeptical enterprise buyer who churned last month'). When omitted, Juno invents a plausible participant for the study.

max_turns.title: Max Turns
max_turns.description: Maximum number of interview turns to simulate. The interview may finish naturally in fewer turns.

SimulationRequest.title: SimulationRequest
SimulationRequest.description: Instruction to simulate a Test-mode interview with a synthetic participant.

ready.title: Ready
ready.description: True only when the simulation completed and the transcript is final.

turns.title: Turns
turns.description: The sample transcript so far, oldest first. Grows while the simulation runs; final once status is 'completed'. Simulated interviews are a Test-mode action — they use no credits, provide no analysis or exports, and never appear as real participant interviews.

error.title: Error
error.description: Why the simulation failed, when status is 'failed'.

SimulationStatusOut.title: SimulationStatusOut
SimulationStatusOut.description:
Derived simulation status plus the transcript accumulated so far.

``turns`` is populated incrementally while the simulation runs, so callers
can render the conversation live from a plain polling loop; once ``status``
is ``completed`` the transcript is final.

speaker.title: Speaker
speaker.description: Who is talking: 'interviewer' is Juno running the study's real interview; 'participant' is the synthetic respondent.

text.title: Text
text.description: What was said in this turn.

turn_number.title: Turn Number
turn_number.description: 1-based interview turn index, when the runtime reports one.

SimulationTranscriptTurn.title: SimulationTranscriptTurn
SimulationTranscriptTurn.description: One spoken turn of a simulated interview transcript.

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.description: Plain-language instruction from the user: the research goal, intended participants, and what the user wants to learn — or, when updating, what to change. A sentence or two is enough.

file_ids.title: File Ids
file_ids.description: Optional file ids from POST /v1/api/files. Include them when documents are part of Create a study or Update a study.

StudyGuidanceRequest.title: StudyGuidanceRequest
StudyGuidanceRequest.description:
Plain-language instruction Juno creates or updates a study from.

Used by both POST /v1/api/studies (create) and POST
/v1/api/studies/{study_id}:refine. The latter technical path means Update a
study. Guidance is free text — what the user would tell Juno — never a
structured design patch.

mode.title: Mode
mode.description: The study's lifecycle value after the change.

url.title: Url
url.description: Absolute invite URL. Durable — the same link across every lifecycle change.

StudyModeOut.title: StudyModeOut
StudyModeOut.description: Result of a lifecycle change: the settled value plus the invite link.

mode.title: Mode
mode.description: Target lifecycle value. 'test' and 'live' map to Test mode and Live mode; setting 'live' is the API equivalent of Go live and needs the studies:golive scope. 'paused' and 'closed' are technical collection states; 'paused' is only valid from live. Setting the current value is a no-op.

StudyModeRequest.title: StudyModeRequest
StudyModeRequest.description: Instruction to choose Test/Live mode or a technical collection state.

org_id.title: Org Id
org_id.description: The organisation this key belongs to.

org_name.title: Org Name
org_name.description: Human-readable name of that organisation. Clients label a stored connection with this — an id alone makes two connected organisations indistinguishable in a list.

environment.title: Environment
environment.description: API data environment from the key prefix: 'test' or 'live'. This is separate from a study's Test mode or Live mode.

scopes.title: Scopes
scopes.description: Scopes granted to this key, sorted. Calls needing a missing scope are refused.

WhoAmIOut.title: WhoAmIOut
WhoAmIOut.description:
Identity of the presented key: which org, which environment, what it can do.

A standard "whoami" any client can call to discover its own grants — and what
the playground key bar reads to show scopes and disable out-of-scope actions.

ApiKey.description: Juno-issued private-beta org key as a Bearer token (jsk_live_… / jsk_test_…). Request access at https://support.heyjuno.co.
